newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-Atlantic daily power lapses; deferreds flat.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-Atlantic daily power lapses; deferreds flat.

text.p: Electricity prices for Monday delivery in the Mid-Atlantic U.S. tumbled Friday after leaping Thursday on a rally in the natural gas market, forecast of a cold snap and outage of the Limerick 2 nuclear unit.
"We're facing a wind-down," a Houston marketer said.
The cold front, which brought frigid temperatures in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect district overnight, was predicted to stay through Saturday, and begin to move away Sunday.
"They're looking at milder weather. Prices came down from yesterday's crazy levels," said an East Coast dealer.
Firm, peak PJM electricity for Monday fell nearly $15.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) to $27.50-$27.75 from $42.00-$44.00 Thursday. Most deals for firm, peak delivery Monday were scheduled at $26.00-$30.00.
Firm, off-peak PJM power for Monday was assessed near $17.00, the upper end of Thursday's range.
Market players said day-ahead PJM prices could weaken further next week with projected lower-than-normal power usage due to the Christmas holiday.
NYMEX January Henry Hub natgas futures were last up 9.6 cents per million British thermal units at $4.505, erasing an early 13.9 cent loss.
Swing gas prices at the Philadelphia city gate were quoted in the mid-$5.00/mmBtu area against Thursday's $5.30-$5.50.
The 1,055 megawatt (MW) Limerick 2 nuclear generating unit in Pottsdam, Pa., which was shut Wednesday to repair a leaking seal, was still planned to resume operation over the weekend.
A 600 MW unit at the coal-fired Homer City, Pa., power station, which was shut Monday due to a oil feed pump problem, was expected to startup today.
January/February 1997 PJM power deliveries were pegged at $31.30-$31.50, down from Thursday's $31.50-$32.00 with deals heard done today in the $31.40-$31.60 range..
March PJM deliveries were assessed at $25.40-$25.70, a tighter range than $25.25-$25.90 Thursday.
First-quarter 1997 PJM was notationally assessed at $29.50-$30.00, flat from Thursday.
July/August 1997 PJM power was assessed at $31.80-$32.10, off slightly from Thursday's $31.90-$32.15.
Third-quarter 1997 PJM held at $29.00-$29.25, and fourth-quarter 1997 PJM remained at $24.00-$24.50.
Calendar 1997 for peak hour delivery in PJM was steady at $26.40-$26.70.
